reasoning: Recent polling over the last month shows a narrowly Democratic-leaning environment in the **Texas 2026 U.S. Senate race**, with most public polls giving James Talarico a small edge over Ken Paxton, typically in the low single digits, though one recent survey has Paxton up by 1 and another finds the race effectively tied.[1][2][3][5][6][9][11] There is no credible, state-specific general-election presidential polling in Texas for the 2026 cycle in the last 45 days, so the best current margin indication is for the Senate race, which averages to roughly a **D+2–3** environment based on recent polls, in contrast to Texas’s structural **R+5** Cook Partisan Voting Index.[1][2][3][5][6][9][11][12]

sources.name: The Texas Tribune (Texas Public Opinion Research)
sources.details: Texas Public Opinion Research poll of 1,048 likely Texas voters finds James Talarico at 45% and Ken Paxton at 40%, a Talarico lead of 5 points in the Texas U.S. Senate race.

sources.name: USA Today (Fox News poll)
sources.details: Fox News poll of 1,006 Texas registered voters shows Talarico leading Paxton 51% to 48% in the Texas U.S. Senate race, a 3-point Democratic advantage within the ±3% margin of error.

sources.name: USA Today (Texas Southern University Barbara Jordan Center)
sources.details: Texas Southern University’s Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research and Survey Center poll of 1,200 likely Texas voters finds Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 45%, a 2-point Talarico lead in the Senate race, within the ±2.83% margin of error.

sources.name: USA Today (Bush School/ReconMR Texas Pulse)
sources.details: ReconMR/Bush School Texas Pulse poll of 619 likely voters shows Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 43% in the Texas Senate race, a 4-point Talarico advantage.

sources.name: Axios (Texas Southern University Barbara Jordan Center)
sources.details: Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research and Survey Center poll summarized by Axios shows Talarico leading Paxton 47% to 45% in the Texas U.S. Senate race, a 2-point Democratic edge.

sources.name: New York Post (Fox News poll / RealClearPolitics aggregate)
sources.details: Fox News Texas Senate poll report notes Talarico at 51% and Paxton at 48% among registered voters, giving Talarico a 3-point lead; article also references a small RealClearPolitics average edge for Talarico of about 0.9 points.

sources.name: Fox 7 Austin (Texas Public Opinion Research)
sources.details: Fox 7 Austin coverage of Texas Public Opinion Research poll reiterates Talarico’s 45% to 40% lead over Paxton in the Texas U.S. Senate race, describing the 5-point margin as outside the poll’s ±3.4% error.

sources.name: The Texas Tribune (poll tracker)
sources.details: Texas Tribune Senate poll tracker summarizes a series of late-July polls showing Talarico slightly ahead of Paxton, and notes a most recent survey where Paxton leads by 1 point, indicating a volatile but very close race.

sources.name: Houston Public Media
sources.details: Houston Public Media overview of the Senate race reports that most recent polling shows Talarico and Paxton in a statistical dead heat, underscoring how narrow the gap is.
sources.date_range: August 2026 (field dates not fully specified, likely early August)

sources.name: Federal News Network (prediction markets overview)
sources.details: Federal News Network summary of Texas Senate prediction markets notes that while current polling indicates a dead heat, prediction market pricing favors Paxton with around 57% implied probability versus Talarico in the low-to-mid 40s.

sources.name: Emerson College Polling/Nexstar Media
sources.details: Emerson College Polling/Nexstar Media survey of Texas likely voters finds Paxton at 47% and Talarico at 46% in the U.S. Senate race, effectively a 1-point Republican lead with 5% undecided and 2% backing others.

sources.name: Cook Political Report PVI Map
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s PVI map lists Texas with a statewide partisan voting index of R+5, indicating the state votes about five points more Republican than the national average in recent presidential elections.
